result.stdout:
Toast Language CLI Tool

Usage:
  toast                                      Start interactive REPL mode
  toast <script.toast>                       Execute a Toast script file
  toast -e <code>                            Evaluate inline Toast code string
  cat script.toast | toast                   Execute script from stdin

Module Management:
  toast module install <url|path> [--name n] Install a module globally
  toast module list                          List all available modules
  toast module uninstall <name>              Uninstall a global module

Options:
  -v, --version                              Display version information
  -h, --help                                 Display this help message
  -e, --eval <code>                          Evaluate inline script code
  -t, --tokens                               Print token stream for script or code
  -a, --ast                                  Print AST structure for script or code
  --lsp                                      Start the Toast Language Server

Examples:
  toast
  toast main.toast
  toast -e "var x = 10; x * 2"
  toast module install https://example.com/vector.dll
  toast module list
  toast module uninstall vector

=== Toast Modules ===

[System Modules] (Protected)
  * system       - System bundle providing all built-in modules (default, object, flow, string, list, utility, converter, import)
  * default      - Default primitive operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise, literals, pipeline, quote)
  * object       - Variable declarations, assignments, object member access, and type definitions.
  * flow         - Control flow commands (if, else, while, for, try, catch, throw)
  * converter    - Standard type converters between Toast types.
  * import       - Module loading command (import).
  * math         - Standard math operations and functions (sqrt, floorDiv, PI, E, operators)
  * datetime     - Date and time manipulation module
  * string       - String manipulation functions and extension methods.
  * list         - List collection operations and algorithms (map, filter, reduce, sort, etc.)
  * utility      - Standard IO, random, and execution utilities.
